author: Blyth, 1845

months.note: 겨울에는 평지로 내려오고 여름에는 중부 이상으로 올라간다.

summary: 활엽수림이나 혼효림에서 볼 수 있는 텃새로, 예전에는 흔했으나 지금은 비교적 드물다. 겨울에는 평지로 내려오지만 여름에는 중부 이상으로 올라가 쉽게 찾아볼 수 없다. 한배에 알을 3~5개 낳고, 딱정벌레를 비롯한 여러 곤충의 어른벌레와 애벌레를 잡아먹는다. 국내에서는 경기도 광릉, 지리산 등지에 분포한다.

points.en: small red streaks at the sides of the hind crown (male)
grey-brown upper cheeks and lower ear-coverts

sexes.male: 뒷머리 양쪽에 작은 붉은 세로무늬가 있다.
sexes.female: 뒷머리 양쪽에 붉은 무늬가 없고, 그 밖에는 수컷과 비슷하다.

art.subject: Grey-capped Pygmy Woodpecker (Dendrocopos canicapillus), adult male, as seen in Korean broadleaf and mixed woodland in winter: forehead and crown brownish-grey; hind crown and nape black; a tiny red streak on each side of the rear crown (male only); a broad white stripe from behind the eye down the side of the neck; lores brownish-white; upper cheeks and lower ear coverts grey-brown; a white moustache stripe; throat whitish; upper back black, the centre of the lower back white with black bars, forming a pale barred patch; wings black with rows of white spots on the coverts and both edges of the flight feathers; underparts dirty whitish-buff with dark brown streaks; short black tail; short grey chisel-tipped bill; dark eye; slender olive-grey legs.
art.pose: clinging to a branch, probing the bark for insects and larvae
art.scene: Korean lowland broadleaf and mixed woodland in winter; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging to a branch: brownish-grey crown, black hind crown with a tiny red streak at its side, white stripe behind the eye, grey-brown ear coverts, black upper back and white lower back barred black, black wings spotted white, streaked buffish underparts, olive-grey legs
adult female, head detail in side view: brownish-grey crown and black hind crown with no red at the sides, white stripe behind the eye, grey-brown ear coverts, short grey chisel bill
art.build: Tiny woodpecker, about the size of a sparrow; compact and short-tailed, with a rounded head. Bill short, straight and chisel-tipped, shorter than the head. Legs short and slender, olive-grey, with two toes forward and two back. Creeps along thin branches and twigs, often on their underside, bracing on its short, stiff, pointed black tail. Wings rounded; flight bounding.
avoid: Do not paint a red crown, a red nape patch or red undertail coverts (Great Spotted and White-backed Woodpeckers); the male's red is only a tiny streak at the side of the rear crown.
Do not paint large white oval shoulder patches (Great Spotted Woodpecker).
Do not make it larger than a sparrow or give it a long bill.
Do not paint a plain brown or plain black back; the upper back is black and the lower back white with black bars.
